biggest_catch: Testbirds' official tester terms say pay is whatever is specified per project — no concrete current pay figure is published anywhere on the official domain.
catches: Official tester terms state the tester is an independent contractor who freely chooses projects.
Pay is defined only as the remuneration specified in each project/order — no standard rate is published.
Payment requires client approval, which can delay or deny payouts.
No current official pay figure exists to anchor the route's earnings claim.

c1.evidence: Testbirds is a real operating company; the tester terms live on the official nest.testbirds.com domain.

c2.evidence: Official tester terms (nest.testbirds.com/terms) exist but define pay only as the per-project remuneration — no concrete figure.

c3.evidence: No upfront fee to join as a tester.

c4.evidence: No concrete current official pay figure on the Testbirds domain; third-party store listings mention ~€20/£15 per regular test but are not official provider-domain terms.

eligibility: Sign up as a tester; accept projects at will as an independent contractor. No official eligibility pay terms published.
notes: Checked 2026-09-23. Official tester terms confirm independent-contractor status, free choice of projects, per-project remuneration, and approval-based payment — but publish no concrete pay amount. A Google Play listing from the official publisher mentioned ~€20/£15 per regular usability test, which was not used since it is not official provider-domain terms. Reject: no concrete official pay figure.
